title: Add prompt: ci-gate-diagnosis
summary: ## Problem or Use Case CI/CD pipeline failures can be frustrating and time-consuming to debug. Failures might be due to flaky tests, environment issues, dependency problems, configuration errors, or actual bugs. Understanding why a gate failed and whether it's a real issue or flake is crucial for maintaining pipeline reliability. ## Proposed Solution Add `ci-gate-diagnosis-prompt.md` to the `devops-deploy/` category. The prompt should: - Analyze CI logs to understand the failure root cause - Distinguish between flaky failures and genuine bugs - Identify if the failure is related to the changes in the PR or pre-existing - Check for common issues (dependency versions, environment differences, timing issues) - Suggest fixes or workarounds with evidence - Recommend whether to retry, fix the code, or fix the pipeline - Provide clear diagnosis with supporting log excerpts ## Expected Benefits - **Faster debugging**: Quickly identify root cause of CI failures - **Reduced flake impact**: Distinguish flakes from real issues - **Better pipeline reliability**: Fix underlying issues, not just symptoms - **Time savings**: Avoid guessing and repeated failed runs - **Improved developer experience**: Less frustration with CI ## Alternatives Considered Manual log analysis is tedious and error-prone. An AI agent can parse complex logs, correlate failures, and identify patterns. ## Additional Context This is particularly valuable for teams with complex CI pipelines or high flake rates.

title: UX: Diagnostic instructions create frustrating knowledge graph for user
summary: On https://mathua.com/onboard -- the instruction is "select what you want to learn". Following this instruction, this was my experience: 1. In my formal education I mastered calculus but nothing beyond, so I want to learn all of the domains following this -- linear algebra through real analysis. I selected only those domains ("what I want to learn"), and completed the diagnostic. 2. This diagnostic unlocked a number of concepts within the selected domains, but left all of the prerequisite domains locked. 3. When learning one of the unlocked concepts, I found myself missing some prerequisite definitions -- for example I can learn `graph.complement` because I have a basic understanding of edges and vertices, but I don't know how to answer a question because I don't know the technical definition of a "simple graph" nor how to find the maximum number of possible edges for one. 4. Navigating the graph further to try to find a concept that would fill in this information, I found these lessons and practice all to be locked because I lacked the prerequisites. I could of course manually go back and master all of the prerequisite concepts to unlock the ones I sought to clarify for myself (`discrete.graphs.basics`), but the more appropriate course of action is to do the onboarding again for all of the domains I learned in high school. This is not made clear from the instruction on the onboarding page. One potential fix would be to maintain a domain DAG and have prerequisite domains auto-selected when choosing a domain like "Graph Theory" for example, so that the diagnostic properly unlocks or at least evaluates all of the prerequisite concepts, thus avoiding the frustrating scenario I experienced.
